reading.title: Tomás and the Last Place Ribbon
reading.purpose: Follow a nervous runner and notice the different ways people speak around him.
paras: On the morning of the school race, Tomás woke up nervous. At the starting line, he began to stammer, repeating the first sound of his own name. His friend Aisha leaned close and murmured to him so softly that only he could hear. "Breathe, and just run your best."

The whistle blew, and the runners shot forward. A boy near the fence bellowed in a deep, loud voice, "Go, Lena!" Then Tomás tripped over his own shoelace. The crowd began to gasp, drawing in a quick breath all at the same time. He sat in the dirt and felt his face burn.

Coach Reyes hurried over. "I want to quit," Tomás muttered, so low that she had to lean down to hear. "Not today," the coach declared in a clear, firm voice. Aisha ran along the fence and pleaded, "Please get up! You have practiced all month."

Tomás stood up, tied his shoe, and walked, then jogged, to the finish line. A boy by the water cooler blurted out that Tomás had lost, without thinking first. "He did not lose!" Aisha protested. "He finished!" Tomás grinned and exclaimed, "I did!"
At the end of the day, every runner who crossed the line got a ribbon. Tomás hung his ribbon above his bed.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, Tomás "muttered" that he wanted to quit. This means he
choices: shouted it loudly so the whole crowd could hear him
said it in a low voice that was hard to hear
wrote it on a small card and handed it to the coach
laughed as he said it to his friend Aisha nearby
qs.why: The next words explain it: he spoke "so low that she had to lean down to hear."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what went wrong for Tomás during the race?
choices: The whistle blew, and the runners shot forward.
He sat in the dirt and felt his face burn.
Then Tomás tripped over his own shoelace.
qs.why: The shoelace is what made him fall. The other sentences tell what happened before or after.

ev.text: Then Tomás tripped over his own shoelace.

qs.q: Why does Aisha protest when the boy says Tomás lost?
choices: She wants the boy to run in the next race instead.
She thinks the coach will give Tomás a second turn.
She is upset that the boy was too loud near the finish line.
She believes finishing the race is a brave thing to do.
qs.why: Aisha says, "He finished!" She thinks finishing after a fall matters more than being first.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this story?
choices: Friends can help you keep trying after you stumble.
Races are won by the runners who cheer the loudest.
A coach should never let a runner stop in the middle of a race.
Nervous people should stay home on the day of a race.
qs.why: Aisha and the coach encourage Tomás, he finishes, and he is proud of his ribbon.

clues.text: so softly that only he could hear
drawing in a quick breath all at the same time
